articles.title: Thirteen-Year-Old Boy Stabbed at Taco Bell in Rochdale, Two Teenagers Arrested
articles.excerpt: A 13-year-old boy has been seriously injured after being stabbed at a Taco Bell in Rochdale town centre. Two teenage boys have been arrested in connection with the incident, which occurred on Riverside Walk.

A 13-year-old boy has been seriously injured following a stabbing at the Taco Bell restaurant on Riverside Walk in Rochdale town centre on Saturday, August 29, 2026. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) received reports of the incident at 6:09 PM and dispatched officers to the scene, where they found the boy with serious injuries. He was subsequently taken to hospital for treatment.

Two teenage boys have been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. They remain in custody as police continue their investigations. Eyewitness accounts suggest that the stabbing occurred in the restaurant's toilets during a chaotic scene involving a group of youths, some reportedly armed with knives. An air ambulance was also deployed to the area in response to the incident.

In response to the stabbing, GMP has increased police presence in Rochdale town centre to restore peace and reassure the community. Chief Inspector Michael Barton stated that officers would be patrolling the area throughout the Bank Holiday weekend, particularly in response to reports of gang activity. Enhanced stop-and-search powers have been authorised to help manage the situation.

The investigation is ongoing, with detectives reviewing CCTV footage and gathering witness statements to understand the circumstances surrounding the attack. Police have urged anyone with information to come forward as they work to identify all individuals involved.

articles.title: Oldham Defeats Rochdale Hornets 32-14 in Season Finale
articles.excerpt: Oldham secured a hard-fought victory over Rochdale Hornets with a score of 32-14 in their final match of the season at Crown Oil Arena, showcasing a strong performance in front of a lively crowd.
articles.content_html:
Oldham Roughyeds triumphed over Rochdale Hornets with a score of 32-14 in a closely contested derby match held at Crown Oil Arena on Sunday, August 30, 2026. The match marked the last game of the season for the Hornets, who played in front of a four-figure crowd eager to support their team.

The Hornets opened the scoring just three minutes into the match when Dan Nixon capitalised on a high kick from Jack Hansen, securing the first try. However, Rochdale's Jordan Paga had a try disallowed shortly after due to an offside in the build-up, which could have doubled their lead.

Oldham responded by equalising through Jack Walker, who took advantage of a mistake in the Rochdale defence. Former Hornet Luke Forber then put Oldham ahead with a try just before half-time, followed by another from Ben Davies, which was successfully converted by Ben O'Keefe, giving Oldham a solid lead.

In the second half, Oldham maintained their momentum, and despite a spirited effort from Rochdale, they could not close the gap. The victory secured Oldham's position in the derby and concluded Rochdale's season on a challenging note.

articles.title: Plans for Demolition and Redevelopment of Lower Falinge Estate in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing proposes to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge and replace them with 270 new homes, aiming to improve the area and address housing needs.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has announced plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in the Lower Falinge estate, paving the way for the construction of 270 new homes. The proposed demolition targets the maisonette blocks known as Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zeburgh, and Vaynor, which RBH describes as no longer fit for purpose and having exceeded their lifespan.

The redevelopment aims to enhance the area between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street, with RBH stating that the new housing will provide a net gain of 150 homes. This follows previous demolitions of the Waverley, Exbury, Yarwell, and Abbeydale blocks, which have already reduced the overall housing stock in Lower Falinge. In addition to new homes, RBH plans to improve public spaces and create better connections to Rochdale town centre through the addition of cycle lanes and footpaths.

Before submitting an official planning application to Rochdale Council, RBH has prepared an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) to identify and mitigate potential environmental and social effects of the proposed development. This assessment will address concerns such as demolition noise, dust, construction traffic, and pollution risks.

The redevelopment of Lower Falinge has been ongoing for over a decade, with previous phases initiated after the estate was identified as one of the most deprived areas in England. The only remaining occupied block, Zeburgh, is home to a couple who are part of a campaign group opposing the demolition. However, with most of the flats already vacant, the campaign faces challenges in garnering support. RBH has committed to creating a community with safe, affordable homes that meet the needs of current and future residents, with a planning application expected to be submitted in early autumn.

articles.title: Middleton Teen Highlights Flaws in Care System Amid Alarming Death Rate for Care-Leavers
articles.excerpt: A 17-year-old from Middleton, who entered care at age 10, has shared his challenges with the care system, coinciding with a report revealing that care-leavers face a significantly higher death rate than the general population.
articles.content_html:
A teenager from Middleton, who went into care at the age of 10, has described his struggles with the care system. Hayden, now 17, lived in a children's home until he was 16 before moving to a semi-independent home, where he felt unsafe and ultimately ended up sofa-surfing.

A government-commissioned report has revealed that young adult care-leavers have a death rate approximately four times higher than that of the general population. The report highlights the severe consequences for individuals who often find themselves without adequate support as they transition out of care, a situation referred to as the "care cliff."

Hayden expressed his concerns about the system, stating, "There are many individuals working hard to improve the lives of young people, but the system is fundamentally flawed." He noted that leaving care at 18 often results in the loss of significant support, leaving many young people to navigate their futures alone.

The report calls for urgent reforms to address these issues and improve outcomes for care-leavers. Hayden's experience underscores the need for systemic change to ensure that young people in care receive the support they need as they transition to independence.

The Greater Manchester Police’s Economic and Cyber Crime Unit is organising a series of drop-in events across Rochdale to help residents stay safe online. These events aim to raise awareness about the various forms of cyber crime, which can have serious consequences for victims, including financial loss and identity theft.

According to GMP, cyber crime encompasses a wide range of fraudulent activities, from identity theft and online transaction scams to dating fraud. The police highlighted that millions of cases of fraud and computer misuse are reported annually, many of which could be avoided by adopting better online habits.

Residents are encouraged to attend these events to learn practical steps to protect themselves from becoming victims of cyber crime. Simple measures, such as not sharing passwords or personal information and creating strong, unique passwords, can significantly reduce the risk of falling prey to online scams.

Details of the specific locations and times for the drop-in events have not yet been released, but residents should monitor local announcements for updates. This initiative reflects GMP's commitment to enhancing community safety in the digital age.

articles.title: Construction of New Play Area at Mainway Meadows in Alkrington Underway
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has commenced work on a new play area at Mainway Meadows in Alkrington, Middleton, alongside improvements to two existing play areas, with completion expected in four to five weeks.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has begun construction of a new play area at Mainway Meadows, located between Mainway and Moss Way in Alkrington, Middleton. This project aims to create an inclusive space for children of various ages and abilities, featuring accessible pathways, safety fencing, and a range of play equipment including swings, a slide, seesaw, roundabout, seating, and a children’s picnic table.

The construction of the Mainway Meadows play area is expected to take four to five weeks. This initiative is funded by Middleton Township, which aims to enhance local play facilities and provide a safe environment for families in the community.

In addition to the new play area, improvements are nearing completion at the Sandy Park play area in Alkrington. Councillor Dylan Williams expressed enthusiasm about the new equipment being installed at Kirkway Stocks Play Park, also known as Farmway or Sandy Park, highlighting the council's investment in local recreational facilities.

These developments are part of Rochdale Council's ongoing commitment to improving community spaces and ensuring that children have access to safe and enjoyable play areas. Local families can look forward to the completion of these projects, which will enhance recreational opportunities in the area.
